MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referral Reason: Diagnostic testing for Cystic Fibrosis
Clinical Indication: Suspected Cystic Fibrosis

TEST PERFORMED
CFTR Gene Mutation Analysis by DNA Sequencing

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. Targeted DNA sequencing was performed for CFTR exons 4, 6a, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 19, 20, 21 and partial intron 19. PCR amplification followed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing was utilized. This panel covers approximately 88% of Caucasian CF mutations, 56% of South Asian mutations, and 76% of worldwide mutations.

RESULTS
Gene: CFTR (NM_000492.4)
Result: No pathogenic mutations detected

No sequence variants were identified in the analyzed regions of the CFTR gene.

TECHNICAL NOTES
All targeted exons and the partial intron 19 region were successfully amplified and sequenced with adequate coverage. Quality metrics met laboratory standards with >99% of bases achieving Q30 quality scores.

INTERPRETATION
No mutations were detected in the sequenced CFTR regions. This analysis covered the most common Cystic Fibrosis mutations; however, it should be noted that approximately 2% of Caucasian CF patients may have negative results with this test due to coverage limitations. The absence of detectable mutations does not exclude a diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis, as mutations may be present in regions not covered by this assay.

LIMITATIONS
This test does not detect:
- Mutations in CFTR exons not included in this panel
- Deep intronic variants
- Large deletions or duplications
- Regulatory region variants
- Mutations with allele frequencies below the detection threshold

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. If clinical suspicion for Cystic Fibrosis persists, consider extended mutation analysis at a specialist laboratory, including:
   - Complete CFTR gene sequencing
   - Deletion/duplication analysis
   - Analysis of deep intronic variants
2. Clinical correlation with sweat chloride testing and pulmonary function tests is recommended
3. Genetic counseling may be beneficial to discuss test results and implications

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted name] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
